analysis:
This PR changes only CI and documentation for the trusted PR threat reviewer. It does not touch provider, coordinator or native code. None of the threat-model assets or boundaries (A-001..A-017, TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-009/TB-010/TB-011) are affected.

Workflow (.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml), base vs head:
- The workflow_dispatch pr_number input and its API-resolution step (base 90-115) are removed.
- The preflight input now defaults to true (head 12).
- The review job now runs only on pull_request_target (head 68-69), and its concurrency group uses only the PR number (head 73).
- THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA now comes only from the event (head 128).
- BEDROCK_SCAN_ENABLED drops the dispatch bypass (head 64). Forks still need BEDROCK_SCAN_ALLOW_FORKS, so AWS-credential exposure is narrowed rather than widened.
- Job timeout rises from 20 to 60 minutes (head 55). The scanner deadline is 3000s (head 131), below both the job timeout and the 3600s role duration (head 116).
- Bedrock limits change from a fixed 12 calls / 4096 tokens to a workload policy: up to 500 calls and 16384 output tokens (head 135-137), both overridable via Actions variables.
- The failure summary now says a human review is required (head 177).

Permissions, pinned actions, persist-credentials:false, the default-branch scanner checkout and the clearance gate steps are unchanged. Removing the paid dispatch path reduces attack surface.

The higher Bedrock cost ceiling applies only to same-repo PRs or explicitly allowed forks. It is a maintainer-configurable policy choice, not a demonstrated regression.

The docs (build.md head 258-263, test.md 729-739) and the changelog fragment only describe this behavior.

Controls outside the supplied evidence: rerun suppression, incomplete-review denial of clearance and workload call sizing are implemented in .github/scripts (threat-model-review.py, threat-review-gate.py), which were not supplied. Integration should confirm in those scripts that:
- a rerun (run_attempt>1) performs no paid calls; and
- timeout or incomplete results always fail clearance.

No threat-model update is needed, because CI reviewer infrastructure is outside this model's scope.
